subject: Reserved Commit — throughput guarantee options & staggered start windows
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sana Patel <sana@cobalthealth.com>, Tom Harrington <tom.h@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved Commit — throughput guarantee options & staggered start windows

Hi Sana / Tom —

Thanks for the time last week. Attached is a short options deck with three reserved-commit structures we discussed (12/24/36-month). High-level notes:

- Option A (12 mo): faster start, smaller bucketed GPU pool (8 A100-equivalent slots), 12% list discount, no capacity carryover. Best if you want a fast onramp and minimal term exposure.
- Option B (24 mo): balanced pricing with staged ramp (month 1–3: 30% capacity, month 4–8: 70%, month 9+: 100%), 18% list discount, optional 15% burst pool for 6 months.
- Option C (36 mo): deepest discount + throughput SLA (p95 latency and minimum sustained vCPU/GPU throughput per pool), 22% list discount, allow two soft-start windows inside first 120 days.

A couple of clarifications you asked for that are in the doc:
- Throughput guarantee: we commit to sustained tokens/sec per GPU pool for Options B/C; when we fail to meet the SLO we provide credits or temporary burst capacity. Exact numbers in the appendix.
- GPU sizing: the proposal uses A100-equivalent sizing; we can convert to whatever instance type you prefer (V100, H100) and adjust pricing.
- Start date flexibility: we can hold a soft start window up to 60 days after signature for Option B and 120 days for Option C; beyond that we re-evaluate capacity alignment.

Request: can you confirm whether the procurement team needs a single DocuSign (master PO + signature) or separate SOW and MSA? If you want a 24- vs 36-month tradeoff, we can prepare a single contract with optional 12-month early-exit buydown.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call to run numbers.

Best,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0124

Attachment: RDW_Cobalt_Reserved_Commit_Options_20270510.pdf (PDF, 4 pages)
From: Tom Harrington <tom.h@cobalthealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sana Patel <sana@cobalthealth.com>, procurement@cobalthealth.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved Commit — throughput guarantee options & staggered start windows

Karthik —

Appreciate the deck. A few quick procurement questions from our side:

1) If we pick the 24-month (Option B) with the staged ramp, what is the exact credit measure if Redwood misses the sustained throughput target in month 10 onward? We need a clear $$/token or % credit mechanism.

2) For Option C (36 mo) you mention p95 latency SLOs — can you confirm whether that is measured per-request or per-route? We have a mix of short chat prompts and long-form document synthesis; the latter skew will change token mix.

3) Start date: we are aiming for production traffic the week of Aug 2. What lead time do you need to guarantee the pool live by Aug 2 if we sign by June 1?

4) Discounts: is the 22% on Option C fixed, or can you provide a ladder (e.g., 20% at signature, 22% after 6 months of onnet usage)?

Also attaching our redlines — legal will want a firm credit formula.

Tom
Sr. Director, Cloud Engineering | Cobalt Health
Attachment: Cobalt_Redlines_20270519.docx (Word, 3 pages)
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Tom Harrington <tom.h@cobalthealth.com>, Sana Patel <sana@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved Commit — throughput guarantee options & staggered start windows

Tom / Sana —

Thanks for the clear questions and the redlines. Answers inline below and I summarized changes we'll put into a revised proposal: 

1) Credit mechanism (Option B): we propose 24x7 measurement on sustained throughput per pool (tokens/sec averaged over rolling 1-hour windows). If average tokens/sec falls below the committed threshold for a calendar month, Redwood issues credits equal to (Committed - Observed)/Committed * monthly reserved fee for that pool. Example in appendix. Legal suggested currency-neutral language; we will include the exact formula and a worked example.

2) p95 latency SLO (Option C): measured per-route. We'll include route definitions (chat vs synth) and allow you to map up to 5 route buckets initially. If your token mix shifts materially we can rebalance the committed throughput and re-baseline during the first 90 days (no charge for the first rebaseline).

3) Lead time for Aug 2 start: sign by June 1 + 30 business days usually works for a full dedicated pool allocation and capacity reservation on the default hardware (A100-equivalent). If you need Aug 2 guaranteed and sign on June 1, we recommend selecting the 24-mo with the 15% burst pool enabled for months 1–3 so you have headroom while we ramp the reserved slice. If you want to compress start time to 2 weeks, we can offer a paid rush (one-time onboarding fee) and commit burst capacity subject to availability.

4) Discount ladder (Option C): we can structure it as 20% at signature, bump to 22% after 6 months onnet usage > 75% of committed throughput. Alternatively, you can lock 22% at signature with a higher minimum commit. I'll have Finance model both variations.

Next steps: I'll have Rishi run the token/sec examples and Marissa draft the revised commercial term sheet with the exact credit formula. Lauren will take a look at the redlines for change-tracking.

Would you like a short 30-minute call this week to walk the team through the credit formula and start-date options?

Best,
Karthik

On a related note: Attachment "Cobalt_Redlines_20270519.docx" received and under review.
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sana Patel <sana@cobalthealth.com>, Tom Harrington <tom.h@cobalthealth.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved Commit — throughput guarantee options & staggered start windows

Team —

A few legal observations on the redlines:

- Credit calculation: prefer a deterministic monthly reconciliaton formula (what Karthik suggested). Add an upper bound on credits (e.g., no more than 50% of monthly reserved fee) to keep economics bounded.
- Rebaseline clause: allow one free rebaseline in first 90 days, subsequent rebases may trigger a pricing review but require 30-day notice.
- Soft-start windows: specify that a soft-start consumes no more than one of the two allowed windows for Option C; after that any further delays will roll the start date and may adjust lead times.

I'll track changes and push a redlined contract back to procurement after Rishi/Marissa finalize numbers.

Lauren Bishop
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Sana Patel <sana@cobalthealth.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Tom Harrington <tom.h@cobalthealth.com>
Cc: procurement@cobalthealth.com, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwoodinference.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 15:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved Commit — throughput guarantee options & staggered start windows

Karthik / team —

Thanks — this is helpful. We prefer the 24-month structured ramp (Option B) but want the 22% ladder you mentioned (20% at signature, auto-bump to 22% after 6 months conditional on >75% usage). We also want the 15% temporary burst pool for the first 3 months.

Confirmed: target production week Aug 2. Procurement will sign a single SOW referencing Redwood's standard MSA (we'll route redlines as you suggested). Please send the revised commercial term sheet + DocuSign link; procurement needs the final DocuSign no later than 2027-06-03 to hit our internal approval cycle.

Sana Patel
VP Product & Cloud Operations | Cobalt Health
procurement@cobalthealth.com
